extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders submitting comments on CMS Medicare and Medicaid proposed rules (providers, clinicians, patient advocates, industry, researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and submitting effective public comments on CMS proposed Medicare and Medicaid regulations, focusing on clarity, evidence, procedural compliance, and CMS-specific expectations. Useful for stakeholders who want their comments to inform CMS rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: State your position clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly indicate if you are for, or against, the proposed regulation or some part of it and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure comments based on the order of the rule and cite the section under which your comment belongs, with headings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on sound reasoning and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS regulatory decisions are based largely on law, clinical and scientific evidence, and program experience; reviewers look for reasoning, logic, and good science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the logical basis for your recommendation and connect assertions to legal/clinical/programmatic evidence and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include supporting references but submit only relevant material
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a copy of articles or other references that support your comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit supporting documents (e.g., articles) but ensure they are relevant to the comment; avoid extraneous material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer published, methodologically strong clinical evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Public comments citing published, methodologically strong clinical evidence that assesses the relative magnitude of an intervention or technology's benefits and risk of harm to Medicare beneficiaries or is generalizable to the Medicare population often give CMS instructive and valuable information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide high-quality studies that quantify benefits/harms and explain generalizability to Medicare beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality over quantity
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies make determinations for a proposed action based on sound reasoning and scientific evidence rather than a majority of votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single, well-supported comment may carry more weight than a thousand form letters; focus on strength of argument rather than volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect privacy when submitting medical information
rubrics_metrics.description: To protect privacy when submitting medical information, remove names or other information that would identify patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redact personally identifiable information and any details that could identify individual patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit comments via Regulations.gov (FDMS); alternative mail/courier accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS migrated regulations to the Federal Dockets Management System (FDMS) at Regulations.gov in 2008. CMS continues to accept regulatory comments via mail or courier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary filing is through Regulations.gov/docket; if necessary, mail or courier submissions are also accepted—follow docket instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe comment periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Usually, the docket stays open for comments at least 60 days for regulations, though some comment periods may differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the specific rule's docket for exact open/close dates and submit within the published period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite applicable Medicare statutes and CMS sub-regulatory guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite Medicare statutes (42 U.S.C. § 1395, etc.) and CMS sub-regulatory guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference relevant statutory provisions and prior CMS guidance to ground legal or policy arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with prior CMS reasoning in the preamble
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with prior CMS reasoning in the preamble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address CMS's stated rationale in the proposed rule's preamble—agree, rebut, or propose alternatives with reasons and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantify provider and beneficiary impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide numeric estimates, cost analyses, utilization impacts, or other measurable statements about how the change would affect stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address affected Medicare populations explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Address Medicare populations (rural, dual-eligibles, specific conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss how the proposal will affect subpopulations (e.g., rural beneficiaries, dual-eligibles, patients with particular conditions) and provide evidence where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend specific regulatory language changes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, provide exact proposed edits to regulatory text rather than only high-level suggestions to help CMS consider implementable changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish coding/billing implementation issues from substantive coverage policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between coding/billing implementation and substantive coverage policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether a comment concerns administrative/implementation details (coding, billing) or whether it challenges substantive policy so CMS can address it in the appropriate context.
